question: Will Tadej Pogačar win the 2026 Tour De France?
rules:
This market will resolve to the cyclist that wins the 2026 Tour De France scheduled for July 4, 2026 through July 26, 2026.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed cyclist to win the 2026 Men Elite at the Tour De France per the rules of the UCI, the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

If the 2026 Tour De France is cancelled, or postponed after August 9, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be official information from UCI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.excerpt: The 2026 Tour de France isn’t even halfway over, but Tadej Pogačar carries a 2:42 lead into the first rest day. UAE sport manager Joxean Fernández Matxín told Velo the team had circled stage 6 as the place to land a knockout punch. There are still nearly two weeks left to race, and Matxín cautioned that UAE is taking nothing for granted.

Tadej Pogačar and UAE Team Emirates-XRG have become the latest squad to be struck by failed air-conditioning at the Tour de France during the first rest day. According to Spanish journalist Sergi López-Egea, the hotel where the Emirati team are staying in the Massif Central is experiencing power issues, with the supply cutting out when guests attempt to switch on the air conditioning units.

Tadej Pogačar, who has a 2:42 lead over second-place Jonas Vingegaard, stayed safe in yellow. The relentless heat forced organizers to cut 30 km from the route through the department of Corrèze between Malemort and Ussel.

evidence.publisher: Tour de France / A.S.O. — official rider interview
evidence.excerpt: UAE Team Emirates set the pace for the peloton during part of Stage 9, where Tadej Pogacar retained the Yellow Jersey. “It was a very hard day. I hope tomorrow will be a calm day, with a nice easy spin and some good rest.”

evidence.publisher: Tour de France / A.S.O. — official stage 6 report
evidence.excerpt: The four-time winner of the race attacked on the slopes of the Col du Tourmalet to claim a 23rd stage win, his eleventh in the Pyrenees, his second in this edition. Pogacar kept pushing, covering the final 43 kilometres alone to open massive gaps at Gavarnie-Gèdre. Jonas Vingegaard finished second (+2’38’’), ahead of a small group led by Isaac del Toro (+2’57’’).

evidence.publisher: Tour de France / A.S.O. — official route announcement, “In Crescendo”
evidence.excerpt: The challenge set for the field of the Tour de France between 4 and 26 July was unveiled before an audience of almost 3,500 at the Palais des Congrès de Paris. Following the Grand Départ in Barcelona, the race will pay a visit to each of the five mountain ranges in France. The only individual time trial will take place against the backdrop of Lake Geneva (stage 16). The double finish on the Alpe d’Huez comprises stages 19 and 20.

evidence.publisher: Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) — “Tour de France: Pogačar’s absolute triumph”
evidence.excerpt: As the Slovenian superstar claimed his fourth overall victory at the Tour, he also improved his own record of being the first rider to always place on the podium in his first eight Grand Tours. In the end, the German newcomer stayed in control and on the overall podium: Tadej Pogačar, Jonas Vingegaard (+04’24’’), Florian Lipowitz (+11’09’’).
